body.statement: If \(\tau_n=n\rho_n\to\tau\in[0,\infty)\), then the sixty-vector \(K\Rightarrow Z\), and jointly \(n\widehat\Delta^P_{\ell}\Rightarrow T_{\ell}\), \(n\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}\Rightarrow T_{\ell}\), and \(n\Delta_{\ell}\to\tau(Q_{\ell}-c_{\ell4})\). Hence \(nL^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}\Rightarrow L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}T_{\ell}\); at \(\tau=0\), this limit equals \(L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\{\pi_{\ell3}/(2\pi_{\ell1}\pi_{\ell2})-1/(2\pi_{\ell4})\}\), which need not vanish under unequal shares.
body.justification: Bounded expected counts change the experiment itself, so a Gaussian correction cannot describe the sampling law.
body.gap: Marohn supplies general Gaussian--Poisson experiment transitions but not the smoothed nonlinear DiD statistic or its unequal-share zero-intensity limit.
body.consumer: Sparse panels with zero cells obtain a defined non-Gaussian reference law rather than an invalid Wald approximation.
body.proof_tex:
For each fixed cell, the probability generating function is
\[
\mathbb E s^{K_{\ell j,n}}
=\{1+r_{\ell j,n}(s-1)\}^{n_{\ell j}}.
\]
The common-rarity, coefficient-limit, and role-share assumptions imply
\[
n_{\ell j}r_{\ell j,n}\to\pi_{\ell j}\tau c_{\ell j},
\qquad n_{\ell j}r_{\ell j,n}^2\to0.
\]
Taking logarithms of the generating function therefore gives the limit
\(
\pi_{\ell j}\tau c_{\ell j}(s-1).
\)
Mutual independence and the fixed number of cells yield the joint product-Poisson limit \(K\Rightarrow Z\).

Define
\[
a_{\ell j,n}=n\widetilde r_{\ell j}
=\frac{n(K_{\ell j,n}+1/2)}{n_{\ell j}+1}.
\]
The count-vector convergence and positive share limits give jointly
\[
a_{\ell j,n}\Rightarrow W_{\ell j}=\frac{Z_{\ell j}+1/2}{\pi_{\ell j}}.
\]
Every \(W_{\ell3}\) is strictly positive.  Hence ordinary algebra on the finite-dimensional vector gives
\[
n\widehat\Delta^P_\ell
=\frac{a_{\ell1,n}a_{\ell2,n}}{a_{\ell3,n}}-a_{\ell4,n}
\Rightarrow T_\ell.
\tag{1}
\]

To compare the exact map, first restrict to the event \(\max_{\ell,j}K_{\ell j,n}\le M\).  On that event all \(a_{\ell j,n}\) lie, for large \(n\), in a compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\) depending only on \(M\) and the role-share bounds.  The common-cutoff proof applies verbatim to any such fixed compact coefficient interval, with \(1/n\) as its rarity scale.  Its factorization gives uniformly on the event
\[
nH(a_{\ell1,n}/n,a_{\ell2,n}/n,a_{\ell3,n}/n)
=\frac{a_{\ell1,n}a_{\ell2,n}}{a_{\ell3,n}}+O(u_n^{-2}),
\tag{2}
\]
where now \(u_n=-q(1/n)\to\infty\).  The limiting Poisson vector is tight, so the probability of the complement can be made arbitrarily small by first choosing \(M\) and then taking \(n\) large.  Removing the cutoff in (2) proves
\[
n\widehat\Delta^E_\ell-n\widehat\Delta^P_\ell\to_P0.
\]
Together with (1), this proves the two statistic limits jointly.

For the population target, exact factorization and the uniform coefficient result give
\[
H(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3})
=\rho_nQ_{\ell n}\{1+O(u_n^{-2})\}.
\]
Because \(n\rho_n\to\tau<\infty\), coefficient convergence yields
\[
n\Delta_{\ell n}
=n\rho_n(Q_{\ell n}-c_{\ell4,n})+o(1)
\longrightarrow\tau(Q_\ell-c_{\ell4}).
\]
Averaging (1)--(2) over fixed \(L\) gives the asserted aggregate limit.  If \(\tau=0\), every limiting Poisson variable is zero, so
\[
W_{\ell j}=\frac1{2\pi_{\ell j}},
\qquad
T_\ell=\frac{\pi_{\ell3}}{2\pi_{\ell1}\pi_{\ell2}}
-\frac1{2\pi_{\ell4}}.
\]
Its average is the displayed deterministic limit and can be nonzero when the four shares differ.
